## correct_answer

## answer_a
Bacteria

## explanation_a
Incorrect. Bacteria, viruses and protozoa are each explicitly included in the governed microorganism list; plants are not. The supported answer is D, Plants.

## answer_b
Viruses

## explanation_b
Incorrect. Bacteria, viruses and protozoa are each explicitly included in the governed microorganism list; plants are not. The supported answer is D, Plants.

## answer_c
Protozoa

## explanation_c
Incorrect. Bacteria, viruses and protozoa are each explicitly included in the governed microorganism list; plants are not. The supported answer is D, Plants.

## answer_d
Plants

## explanation_d
The major microorganism groups include bacteria, fungi, protozoa, helminths and viruses; plants are not in that microorganism list. The official MUST teaching directly supports Plants for this prompt. Therefore D is retained as the unchanged source-printed answer, pending medical review.

## correct_answer

## answer_a
Cause diseases in humans

## explanation_a
Incorrect. Saprophytes are not defined by causing human disease, obligate intracellular replication or antibiotic production. The supported answer is B, Decompose dead organic matter.

## answer_b
Decompose dead organic matter

## explanation_b
Saprophytes feed on dead animal or plant material and thereby decompose dead organic matter. The official MUST teaching directly supports Decompose dead organic matter for this prompt. Therefore B is retained as the unchanged source-printed answer, pending medical review.

## answer_c
Reproduce inside living cells

## explanation_c
Incorrect. Saprophytes are not defined by causing human disease, obligate intracellular replication or antibiotic production. The supported answer is B, Decompose dead organic matter.

## answer_d
Produce antibiotics

## explanation_d
Incorrect. Saprophytes are not defined by causing human disease, obligate intracellular replication or antibiotic production. The supported answer is B, Decompose dead organic matter.

## correct_answer
B

## answer_a
Species

## explanation_a
Incorrect. The species name follows the genus and is not capitalized; family and class are not the two-name position asked by this item. The supported answer is B, Genus.

## answer_b
Genus

## explanation_b
In scientific nomenclature the genus is the first name and is capitalized, while the following species name is not capitalized. The official MUST teaching directly supports Genus for this prompt. Therefore B is retained as the unchanged source-printed answer, pending medical review.

## answer_c
Family

## explanation_c
Incorrect. The species name follows the genus and is not capitalized; family and class are not the two-name position asked by this item. The supported answer is B, Genus.

## answer_d
Class

## explanation_d
Incorrect. The species name follows the genus and is not capitalized; family and class are not the two-name position asked by this item. The supported answer is B, Genus.

## title
The main structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells is:

## question
The main structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells is:

## subject
inf

## status
Draft

## owner
Dr. Omar

## vignette


## format
single best answer

## derived_from
Transcribed verbatim from src_4bd3b78f762673d7eb7f; printed key checked against src_88ddfa49fe01adee5444 without treating the student bank as an authenticated faculty key.

## correct_answer
A

## answer_a
Presence of a nucleus

## explanation_a
Prokaryotic cells lack a true nucleus and nuclear membrane, whereas eukaryotic cells have a true membrane-bound nucleus. The official MUST teaching directly supports Presence of a nucleus for this prompt. Therefore A is retained as the unchanged source-printed answer, pending medical review.

## answer_b
Presence of a cell wall

## explanation_b
Incorrect. A cell wall is not the universal separator in the offered comparison, and both cell types can reproduce. The supported answer is A, Presence of a nucleus.

## answer_c
Ability to reproduce

## explanation_c
Incorrect. A cell wall is not the universal separator in the offered comparison, and both cell types can reproduce. The supported answer is A, Presence of a nucleus.

## answer_d
None of the above

## explanation_d
Incorrect. A cell wall is not the universal separator in the offered comparison, and both cell types can reproduce. The supported answer is A, Presence of a nucleus.
